prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear about the accident — that’s stressful. I can help you decide which type of lawyer to hire and how to pick a good one in Pleasanton, CA. A few quick questions first (optional): how badly were you hurt, was fault clear, when did the crash happen, have you talked to an insurance company, and do you want me to find specific local attorneys now?

If you want immediate steps
- Get medical care now and keep records (doctor notes, bills, imaging). Even if injuries seem minor, some show up later.
- Call the police and obtain the collision report or report number.
- Photograph the scene, damage, injuries, and any visible vehicle debris.
- Get witness names/contacts.
- Preserve evidence (vehicle, clothing) and note repair shop estimates.
- Don’t admit fault or speculate about causes to other drivers or insurers.

Important deadlines (California)
- Personal injury lawsuit: generally 2 years from the date of the injury (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 335.1).
- If the claim is against a government entity (city, county, state), you generally must file an administrative claim within 6 months — much shorter.
Missing deadlines can bar your case, so act promptly.

Which lawyer to hire — the right type
- Hire a personal injury attorney who handles car-accident cases (not a general practice lawyer).
- If severe injury, permanent impairment, or complex liability (commercial vehicles, DUI, multiple vehicles), look for a lawyer with trial experience and resources to investigate.

How to find and evaluate lawyers
- Look locally: Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, San Ramon, Walnut Creek; many firms serve the Tri-Valley.
- Check: State Bar of California (discipline record), client reviews, peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), and firm results (settlements/verdicts).
- Ask for results in similar cases (comparable injuries/facts), how many cases they take to trial, and whether they’ll handle all work in-house or refer out.

Questions to ask in the free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident cases in Pleasanton/Alameda County? How many per year?
- What is your experience with cases like mine? Any verdicts/settlements I should know about?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- What do you estimate is my case worth (range) and how long might it take?
- What is your fee structure and what costs will I be responsible for? (See note below)
- Will you advance experts’ costs?
- How often will you update me and by what method?

Fee structure — what to expect
- Most car-accident injury lawyers work on contingency: they get a percentage of the recovery if you win; no recovery = no attorney fee.
- Typical contingency splits in California: about 33.3% (one-third) if settled before lawsuit, 40% if taken to trial; some firms use sliding scales or different numbers. Also ask who pays case costs (they may be advanced and reimbursed from recovery).
- Confirm in writing exactly how fees and costs will be handled.

Red flags when interviewing
- Pressure to sign immediately.
- Guarantees about outcomes or specific settlement amounts.
- Unwillingness to put the fee agreement in writing.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about experience.

Where to look / referral sources
- State Bar of California Lawyer Referral Service.
- Alameda County Bar Association’s lawyer referral service.
- Local consumer review sites (Google/Yelp), Avvo, and Martindale-Hubbell.
- Recommendations from people you trust or other attorneys (e.g., family attorney).

What to bring to your first meeting
- Police report number or copy, photos, medical records or summaries, insurance information (yours and other driver’s), witness contact info, and any correspondence from insurers.

If you want, I can:
- Look up 3–5 Pleasanton-area car-accident attorneys with good reviews and show you contact details and key points to compare.
- Draft a short email or call script for contacting lawyers or insurers.
Tell me whether you want local attorney names now and give any case specifics you’re comfortable sharing.
